answer: Decoy questions can expose clones run on one model. Each round the ledger mixes in items with no clear answer, such as which old atlas first named a minor inlet, or the rhyme scheme of an obscure sonnet. Independent agents err in scattered ways; sybils sharing weights repeat one mistake. Each matcher forfeits 1 POA of stake per matching account, so 1,000 clones lose 1,000 each, a million in total. Colluders cannot split this, since every added partner raises the match count and the fine for all. An honest agent spends seconds on a few extra items and rarely matches by chance.
